environment.cpu: AMD Ryzen 7 Pro 7735U with Radeon Graphics
environment.biasNotes: Linux/ext4 only, per the 2026-07-26 scope narrowing. Development machine; latency and startup thresholds remain hypotheses until a real-hardware pass (A2).

method: Tauri 2 host on WebKitGTK, UI served at runtime over a custom URI scheme; readiness reported by the page through the sink command. Summed process-tree RSS sampled from /proc. AT-SPI exposure probed via pyatspi when available, UNKNOWN when not. SCOPE: Linux/ext4 only; latency and startup gates are hypotheses until a real-hardware pass.

omitted_gates.reason: flat-list concept: it reads the single consistent aria-setsize the rows advertise, else 0. A tree advertises per-sibling-group setsize, so it collapses to 0 and would contradict a11y_tree_structure on the same dump. Superseded by a11y_tree_structure.

omitted_gates.gate: latency, stall, cliff, peak RSS trend
omitted_gates.reason: the run is a couple of minutes of real pointer and keyboard input, not a soak; it has nothing true to say about frame cadence or a leak slope.

scope.input: Real X input throughout: xdotool clicks on the shipped outline bar and the shipped navigator rows, and xdotool keystrokes. The page's own JavaScript is never called, and app/ui/src/project.ts's exported outline unit is never touched.
scope.button_geometry: The bar's four buttons are located through the AT-SPI component extents, not computed from a stylesheet. At their natural widths they occupy 8..271 px of the 280 px navigator column; any fixed width wide enough for "New chapter" pushes the fourth past the column edge, where #editor paints over it and it stops being clickable. The rig aborts if a button is missing from the accessibility tree, advertises the wrong accessible name, or centres outside the column. Navigator ROW coordinates stay computed from the store's own walk, as switch-cli.ts computes them.
scope.create_row_delta: Mounted AT-SPI tree rows before and after the create. At the tiny fixture the whole projection (40 rows) fits the 900px window, so mounted == projected; the run aborts if the pre-create probe does not mount every row, because the metric would otherwise be counting the window rather than the projection.
scope.create_kept_open_doc: Nothing reports which document the editor holds. Read instead as: the sentence typed AFTER the create is in the scene that was open BEFORE it. A rebuilt page reopens the boot-time document, so the sentence would land elsewhere. A remount that happened to reopen the same document is indistinguishable from a repaint by this or any other external observation.
scope.mutation_latency: Measured from the input event returning to the store file showing the change, polled every 2 ms against a second read-only connection. It therefore INCLUDES X event delivery and the page's handler, and EXCLUDES the walk re-read and reprojection that follow the command - the gate's threshold text names the whole round trip, and no external observer can see its tail at this resolution (an AT-SPI probe costs hundreds of milliseconds). The hierarchy run's in-page mutation_p95_ms is the comparable number for the command itself. Three samples, so p50 and p95 are order statistics over three values, not percentiles.
scope.rename_and_reorder: Both read from the file the killed process left behind, so they say the edit reached the store and survived the kill, not merely that the screen redrew. reorder_position_match compares the ordinal the store held before the kill against the reopen boot's OWN projection of the same file, which is a second process's derivation rather than a second read of the first's.
scope.reopen_boot: APP_PERSIST_MODE=write with APP_MUTATIONS=0, because the verify payload returns before the tree block is built and carries no walk. Its 1 s soak types into whichever scene it opens, which is why every title and body above is read from the file BEFORE this boot runs.

verdicts.value: 1 row(s) added; new title in the walk; open document unchanged
verdicts.threshold: row count grew by exactly 1, the new title is in the walk, and the editor still holds the item id it held before the create

verdicts.value: new title in the reopened walk
verdicts.threshold: the renamed item carries its new title in the walk read from the reopened file
the reordered item's position among its siblings in the reopened file == the one shown before the kill
text typed before the mutations is byte-identical in the reopened file
